_comment: Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-4.3B: an ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 (16MB quad flash, 8MB octal PSRAM) behind a 4.3-inch 800x480 parallel RGB panel (ST7262) with a GT911 touch controller and a CH422G expander, the same panel electronics as the 7-inch board (esp32-s3-waveshare-touch-lcd-7.json): every RGB line, the sync signals, the I2C bus, the touch INT and the expander lines match pin for pin (vendor wiki, 'ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-4.3B'). Timings are the vendor's shared ESP-IDF demo for the 4.3/7 family. What the B adds sits off the panel: RS485 on the UART0 pins, CAN on GPIO15/16, optically isolated digital I/O on the expander's spare lines, a PCF85063 RTC on the I2C bus and a lithium charger (CS8501) with a 7-36V input. Composed from the chip catalog; not yet verified on hardware.
_console: The USB-C port is the S3's native USB-Serial/JTAG, the base target's default. Unlike the 7-inch board, UART0 (GPIO43/44) feeds the RS485 transceiver here, so there is no second console.
_psram: N16R8 is 8MB octal PSRAM; the RGB panel's framebuffer (800x480x2 = 768KB, plus a back buffer) lives there.
_buses: GT911 touch, CH422G expander and the PCF85063 RTC share the bus. The RTC has no role in a composed definition yet.

display._pins: data0-4 = B3-B7, data5-10 = G2-G7, data11-15 = R3-R7. The backlight (DISP) is EXIO2 on the CH422G, so no GPIO is named here.

touch._pins: Reset is EXIO1 on the CH422G; INT is GPIO4, which the binding also drives low across reset to fix the controller's I2C address at 0x5d.

expander._outputs: EXIO1 touch reset, EXIO2 backlight (DISP), EXIO3 panel reset, EXIO4 microSD chip-select. On the B, EXIO0 and EXIO5 are the isolated digital inputs DI0/DI1 and OD0/OD1 the isolated outputs, none of which a composed board drives. initialOutputs 0x1e as on the 7-inch: resets released, backlight on, card deselected.

_storage: The microSD slot is on SPI (MOSI GPIO11, SCK GPIO12, MISO GPIO13, CS on EXIO4), which the composed base does not drive yet; no storage is declared.
_controls: The BOOT button is GPIO0, which the RGB bus uses as data6 (G3) on this board, so there is no launcher button.
